applicable_when: The kernel performs a channels-last to channels-first layout transposition with bias add. in_ptr0 has strides (290400, 1, 5280, 96): the channel dimension y0 is stride-1 but the spatial dimension x2 is stride-96. With XBLOCK=128, consecutive threads in the warp access in_ptr0 at offsets 96 apart (stride-96 pattern), causing severely uncoalesced loads — only 26.2/32 bytes per sector are used. The L2 is saturated at 96.71% while SM compute is only 27.62%, confirming memory bandwidth is the bottleneck. Increasing YBLOCK (which covers y0 = yindex%96, the stride-1 channel dimension) so that consecutive threads in the Y dimension access consecutive channel elements would improve load coalescing. @triton.autotune will explore configs where YBLOCK is larger relative to XBLOCK, finding the sweet spot between coalescing and occupancy.
